hook: An FBI Los Angeles field office memo transmitting Issue No. 24 of 'Flying Saucers International' — the official journal of the Amalgamated Flying Saucer Clubs of America — after an IRS employee flagged an article purportedly received via shortwave radio from an alien as potential Communist Party propaganda, accompanied by newspaper clippings of 1965–1966 UFO sightings.
why_it_matters: This file documents the FBI treating a civilian UFO publication as a domestic political surveillance matter rather than a national security or aerial phenomenon concern — the trigger was not the UAP content but anti-war, anti-military-industrial-complex messaging attributed to an extraterrestrial source. The inclusion of newspaper clippings alongside the political flagging shows the Bureau was tracking both the subculture and the media coverage simultaneously. The Los Angeles office ultimately declined to open a full investigation, indicating the Bureau found no actionable intelligence.

key_findings.finding: An IRS employee flagged an article in a civilian UFO magazine to the FBI as Communist Party propaganda, prompting an inter-divisional referral from Philadelphia to Los Angeles.

quotes.text: Mr. COOPER stated he subseribed to the magazine because his son had exhibited an interest in fliring saucers and outer space. He said that on pages 2 and 3 of Issue No, 24 was an article which he believed expounded the Commmist Party (CP) line.

key_findings.finding: The article alleged to be Communist propaganda was framed as a message from an extraterrestrial named 'Master Kalen-Li Retan' of the planet Korendor, received via shortwave radio by a civilian named Bob Renaud who claimed to have visited alien undersea bases and piloted spacecraft.

quotes.text: Editor's Note: This special message was received from Master Kalen-Li Retan (head of the planet Korendor, about 400 light years distant) on May 4, 1966 via special directional short-wave radio by Bob Renaud, the young electronic-technician whose remarkable story we printed in issues #18, 19, 20,21, and 22

eventually met his contacts in-person; visited their undersea and underground bases on our planet; was taken aboard many of their spaceships; and was actually allowed to pilot two of their small scout craft — one on a short solo flight.

key_findings.finding: The 'alien message' explicitly claimed the real U.S. government resided in the Pentagon and defense industries rather than elected officials, and alleged President Kennedy was assassinated for opposing the Military-Industrial Complex.

quotes.text: Make no mistake. Your government is not in the White House or the Congress. IT IS IN THE PENTAGON, AND IN THE HEADQUARTERS OF THE VAST "DEFENSE"-ORIENTED INDUSTRIES. It is THEY, not the President or the Congressmen, who run the United States.

This is what happened to the late Mr. Kennedy who, in his great humanitarianism, was reluctant to sacrifice his ideals and his visions for the sake of the Military Industrial octopus. He paid the supreme penalty for his efforts in behalf of humanity.

key_findings.finding: The FBI Los Angeles office found no existing records on the AFSCA or Bob Renaud and closed the matter without opening an investigation.

quotes.text: The indices of the Los Angeles Division contain no informtion identiflable with RENAUD, and no investigation has ever been conducted on captioned organization. No further action is contemplated in this matter by the Los Angeles Office, UACB.

key_findings.finding: The file also contains contemporaneous newspaper clippings documenting civilian UFO sightings from 1965–1966, including the March 1966 Michigan incident involving college students and a deputy, and a 1965 farmer encounter with an egg-shaped craft in Newark Valley, New York.

quotes.text: Newark Valley—Gary T. Wilcox is a young man dogged by rumors People say his dairy farm has gone bust be- cause nothing will grow on the land.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Newspaper clippings in the file reference the Air Force and its investigation programs tracking UFO sighting reports from the same 1966 period.

The alien-attributed article explicitly names Congress and the Pentagon as subjects of its political critique, which was the basis for the CP-line allegation that brought the document to the FBI's attention.
